opportunities.description: dissect (tools/dissect/dissect/extract.py) and rqs (tools/rqs/rqs/scan.py) each walk repositories with their own skip lists, language maps and test-path rules, and each tool has its own MCP stdio loop and error convention. RQS-2030 step 2 already pairs `dissect scan` with `rqs probe`; rqs could read inventory and symbols from a dissect database, and the three servers could share one loop and one error type.

opportunities.title: Scoring parameters as data in the standard
opportunities.description: The core weight, coverage gate, blocking thresholds, grade caps and opportunity confidence weights are prose in standard/rqs-2030.yaml and literals in tools/rqs/rqs/score.py:15,79-80,106,111 (at 0bdc987). Moving them into the YAML as numbers makes the score.py docstring true, lets other implementations score identically, and lets a revision of the standard change scoring without a code change.

opportunities.title: A bounded, dependency-free artifact reader
opportunities.description: tools/rex/rex/formats.py reads ELF, PE, Mach-O, ZIP, npm tgz, ASAR, Go build info and Rust .dep-v0 in 310 lines of standard-library Python, and the research shows it answering questions REA refused (research/dissection/README.md:146-156). Once bounded and fuzzed (gap G3) it is useful on its own to other agent tools; today the missing limits make it unsafe to reuse.

reengineering.component: rex bundle import and artifact readers (tools/rex/rex/store.py, formats.py, probes.py)
reengineering.gain: Clears red line RL-4 and the SEC-8 and REL-2 gaps; 'tampered records are rejected' becomes true for every bundle row.
reengineering.measure: A malicious-bundle and malformed-artifact corpus in tools/rex/tests passes; a fuzz run over formats.py finds no unhandled exception over a stated number of CPU-hours; peak RSS on a 10x-size input stays under a stated cap.

reengineering.component: rqs probes and suggestion rules (tools/rqs/rqs/scan.py, probes.py, suggest.py)
reengineering.gain: Suggestions stop resting on rqs's own tables and the standard's prose, and the evidence they miss today is found.
reengineering.measure: Probing RE4exa yields no found=true probe whose evidence lies only in standard/ or tools/rqs/; on the reviewed set, the share of automatic levels that reviewers keep (rqs agree between template and review) rises against the baseline measured in this campaign.

reengineering.component: Shared core for MCP stdio, errors and repository inventory used by rex, dissect and rqs
reengineering.gain: One error contract and one protocol implementation instead of three hand-written loops of 35-40 lines each.
reengineering.measure: A contract test sending equivalent invalid inputs to all three tools gets the same error shape; line count of the three mcp.py files before and after.

reengineering.component: Repository pipeline: LICENSE, CI and generated claims
reengineering.gain: PRV-3 red line cleared; COR-1 from 1 to 3; EPI-5 from 1 to 3.
reengineering.measure: rqs probe meta.license detects an SPDX license; CI runs the 40 tests and standard/build.py --check on every push on two operating systems; a script regenerates README number tables from results/ and CI fails on any diff.

questions: Does RE4exa meet its own RQS-2030 bar? No: grade D (QI 38.1, coverage 100%), capped by two confirmed red lines (RL-1 no license, RL-4 injection-prone bundle import); its strengths are rex's evidence model, durable steps and small catalogs, its weaknesses the absence of CI, policies, test strength and agent-safety controls.

Do the README claims match the results they cite? For REA's numbers mostly yes (exact matches on catalog bytes, timings, export size, graph counts); for rex's own several do not (4.0 s vs 4.48 s; 'measured fixes' that were not measured; 0.42 s, 52-70 ms and 4,607 bytes with no committed result; 'standard-library Python' vs PyYAML).

How accurate is rqs on its own repository (G14)? Poor: 19 of 85 probes report found=true on rqs's pattern tables or the standard's prose alone, 9 of 39 levelled suggestions rest only on such lines, 2 of 8 suggested flags and the suggested profile are wrong, 17 of the 39 automatic levels had to change, and the real evidence (numeric claims, harness and results, describe commands, the dynamic SQL in rex) is missed.
not_examined: The research harnesses were not re-run (REA package, Postgres crash test, caveman and leanrea lenses, product-eval.py); their committed outputs were checked against the READMEs instead.
Exploitability of the rex import SQL construct and of the parser resource limits was not demonstrated (defensive review rules).

Whether the git subcommands dissect runs inside scanned repositories (tools/dissect/dissect/extract.py:66-70, without the hardening rqs applies at scan.py:372) honour repository configuration that starts programs was not tested.
The exact size of rex's MCP catalog (4,607 bytes claimed) was not recomputed; only the test bound of 12,000 bytes was run.
The dissection database was checked for counts, kinds and secrets only; the 603 claim nodes and the curated layer were not audited one by one.
macOS, Windows and Python 3.11-3.12 behaviour (only Linux with Python 3.13.16 was used).
GitHub-side settings (branch protection, pull-request review) are not visible from the checkout.
The standard's regulatory dates and references were not checked against primary sources (no web access).
scope_notes: Profile agent-tool: RE4exa ships three agent-first CLIs and MCP servers (rex, dissect, rqs) with skills, and the standard itself names rex and dissect as agent-tool examples (standard/RQS-2030.md:94); the suggested workflow-engine came from the word 'durable' (tools/rqs/rqs/suggest.py:61-63). Flags: uses_llm (MCP servers and skills), executes_code (rex ext and run start external programs; dissect runs node, go and git), parses_untrusted (binaries, archives, repositories, bundles), uses_crypto (SHA-256 content addresses verified on import, tools/rex/rex/store.py:209-215); network_service and heavy_compute are off because every probe hit for them is rqs's own pattern table (tools/rqs/rqs/scan.py:151-159), distributed is off (no package, release or tag). Reviewed commit 0bdc987 via git show and git archive; HEAD moved to 82e1713 during the review (review files plus compensated summation in score.py), and validation used that rqs.
